evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bid to withhold MI5 information from Heaton Park attack inquests - BBC News Image source, Family handouts Image caption, Adrian Daulby and Melvin Cravitz, were killed in the attack on the Heaton Park Synagogue in Manchester Published 3 September 2026 The Government has applied to block some MI5 information relating to the fatal Manchester synagogue attack from being heard in public, a court has heard. A pre-inquest hearing at Manchester Coroner's Court was told the Home Office wanted the information to be withheld when the inquests into the deaths of Adrian Daulby, 53, and Melvin Cravitz, 66, are held next year. Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, a Syrian-born British citizen, drove into the gates of the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue in Manchester on 2 October last year. He then began attacking with a knife, while wearing a fake suicide belt. Cravitz died from multiple knife wounds while Daulby was killed by a bullet fired by armed police scrambled to the scene. He was hit as he blocked the synagogue doors to stop Al-Shamie getting in. The hearing earlier was told by Neil Sheldon KC, representing the Home Office, that making public the information held by MI5 would put national security at risk. He said: "The Secretary of State asserts that disclosure would harm national security." But lawyers for the families of the victims said the Government's attempt to withhold the information, through a Public Interest Immunity application, was in "contradiction" to statements made after the attack. The family lawyers cited statements made by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood and counter-terror police bosses that terrorist Al-Shamie was not on their radar and unknown to them. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Union secures £15k towards unpaid Manchester Pride performer fees - BBC News Image caption, Performers' union Equity says its unpaid members were "the heart of Manchester Pride" By Angela Ferguson North West Published 3 September 2026 A trade union representing some of the performers left unpaid after the charity running Manchester Pride went into administration said it has managed to secure £15,000. Equity said the money came from contributions from businesses within the "social action pot" put forward by Manchester City Council. It comes amid an ongoing Charity Commission investigation into the organisation which previously ran the event. Equity member and LGBTQ+ theatre-maker and activist Nathaniel Hall said it was "encouraging" news and, while the money would not cover all the losses, "the gesture is really welcome". Hall said LGBTQ+ Equity members "can be proud they have a union that has their backs when times are tough". The charity previously behind Manchester Pride entered voluntary liquidation in October 2025 . In a statement issued on 12 August, the Charity Commission said they were continuing to liaise with liquidators regarding Manchester Pride and their regulatory compliance case into the charity was ongoing. Image source, Stuart Rhoades Image caption, People have gathered in Manchester for the annual pride event for more than 40 years after its humble beginnings in 1985 Equity said it was contacting more than 50 performers who came forward to say they were owed £70,000. It said it would be distributing a percentage of unpaid fees to each artist, equating to about 20% of what they were owed. They said the funding, coupled with a £12,500 crowdfund sum organised by Nathaniel Hall brought the total raised to £27,500, almost 40% of the money owed. Equity North

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mother has told how her family's lives changed overnight when her son developed life-threatening sepsis at the age of five Archie, from Wigan, Greater Manchester, was diagnosed with meningitis B which developed into sepsis , external and he spent five days in a coma in 2018 He was admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit at the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital, where he received specialist care and rehabilitation before being discharged two weeks later His mother Kate said her son's illness "changed our lives overnight" and seeing him "so seriously unwell and fighting for his life was the most frightening time we have ever experienced as a family" Sepsis is a life-threatening reaction to infection anywhere in the body, where, instead of fighting the bacteria or virus that is making you ill, the immune system turns on itself, damaging internal organs and potentially causing death Now aged 13, Archie continues to receive care at the hospital, attending for regular check-ups, undergoing operations, and receiving physiotherapy and occupational therapy

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Production at Kellogg's Trafford Park factory comes to an end - BBC News Image source, Peter McDermott Image caption, Production is moving to a Kellogg's site in Wrexham in north Wales By Richard Stead , Reporting from in Trafford Park and Angela Ferguson , North West Published 3 September 2026 Production at the Kellogg's factory in Greater Manchester has come to an end after almost 90 years, with the loss of about 360 jobs. The site in Trafford Park was one of the largest cereal factories in Europe when built in 1938 but production is being transferred to the company's site in Wrexham, north Wales. A spokesperson for owners Kellanova said the site has been a crucial part of its success for decades, adding: "We thank everyone who has worked there, as well as the suppliers, partners and local community who have worked alongside us." Mick Murray from retail union Usdaw said it was "a sad time" after working to "try to secure the best possible outcome for our members". In 2024 Kellanova announced that production of breakfast cereals would move to Wrexham, saying the investment required to maintain the factory was not viable. It came after the end of three-month talks with union and employee representatives . Marking the last week of production on site, a company spokesperson said: "A significant milestone was reached this week, as operations across production and packing came to an end." They said their priority through the transition has been to "support colleagues and the wider community through this period of change". Image source, Kellanova Image caption, The Trafford Park site was once one of the largest food manufacturing facilities in Europe Kellogg's is an American company founded in Michigan in 1906. Bev Craig said funding would be made available to all of the boroughs and it would be enough to repair and maintain over a million square metres of road. Craig had promised to repair more roads and make sure pavements were safe during her election campaign. But Rod Dennis from the RAC said what was needed to fix "Britain's pothole woes, and those we see in Manchester, is guaranteed long-term funding over many, many years". Image caption, Funding is being made available to all 10 Greater Manchester boroughs Dennis called for "an end to the kind of patch and dash approach which we've seen some councils employ and proper planning to get the roads back to where they need to be". Craig said 2.5 billion journeys were made across the roads of Greater Manchester every year "and we need to properly invest in them and this is about getting money out of the door quickly to fix the things that people have been complaining to me about". Image caption, Garage owner Dave Rigby says that almost every day he sees drivers bring in vehicles damaged by potholes Dave Rigby, who runs a garage in Eccles, told BBC North West Tonight that potholes were "quite a big factor", with vehicles often brought in there every day for repairs as a result of them. title: Six Greater Manchester Police officers sacked over racist remarks

evidence_packet.title: Six Greater Manchester Police officers sacked over racist remarks
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester Police dismisses six officers over racial language used against a colleague
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police dismisses six officers over racial language used against a colleague
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Six serving police officers have been sacked following an internal investigation by Greater Manchester Police into alleged racial discrimination against a fellow officer GMP said two other former officers who were also investigated would have been fired if they were still on the force. Another officer received written warning A force disciplinary panel heard the female officer of African heritage (who was not named in the proceedings) complained after her accent was mimicked by a group of officers She was also compared to a suspect with similar skin colour, while one officer made a derogatory comment about her hair The panel found six officers and two former officers committed gross misconduct, while a ninth officer was found to have committed misconduct PCs Demi Green, Heena Rani, Lucy Granby, Matthew Barlow, Matthew Hill, and Mohammed Abid - who made the remark about his colleague's hair - were dismissed without notice

evidence_packet.title: I want to give comfort to grieving families, says artist
evidence_packet.lead: Allie Pottinger painted a mural for a hospital maternity unit's bereavement room
evidence_packet.summary: Allie Pottinger painted a mural for a hospital maternity unit's bereavement room
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An artist who has painted a mural in a hospital maternity unit's bereavement room said she "just wanted to bring some comfort" to heartbroken families after the loss of a baby Allie Pottinger created the mural at Macclesfield General Hospital's Bluebell Suite, described as a private and peaceful space where families can begin to grieve and spend time together She said she chose the painting of bluebell woods for its calming properties and solace featuring a gate showing light "to offer some hope" It is the watercolour artist's fourth painting in the hospital, which has a special place in her heart. Her late father was a consultant surgeon for 22 years and her sister also now works there She said she painted her first two murals at the hospital - of Shutlingsloe on the edge of Macclesfield Forest and Porth Diana at Trearddur Bay on the Anglesey coast - with her dad in mind in 2022, the year after his death "I wanted to gift something because he lived and breathed it," said the 60-year-old artist

It can be very difficult,” he told my colleague Declan Carey, who visited the stretch this week While there Declan heard car horns blaring, pedestrians veering wildly into the road and plenty of road rage. Dubbed Manchester’s ‘worst’ road, many shopkeepers told Declan they’ve seen accidents and deaths on the ‘horrendous’ road since the 1990s “It’s one of the worst roads in Manchester, it’s total chaos in the evenings,” the traffic warden adds View 6 Images Traffic chaos Stockport Road in Longsight. Picture Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News (Image: Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News) Data kept by Transport for Greater Manchester points to a major safety problem on Stockport Road. A fatality happened in 2025 at the ever-busy junction with Slade Lane Further up by Stanley Road and Dickenson Road, the area is littered with accident reports, with multiple minor and serious collisions logged since 2024. But can anything really be done to improve things?

Your dad is a judge." Following further visits to the woman's home demanding money, Huo then sent a letter to the other neighbours in the area, about the woman. It read: "Dear neighbour, they [at house number] are paedophiles.... Her father is a judge... Please keep your children safe. From your frien Manchester Crown Court heard that days later the woman woke to sounds of smashing glass. Tahir Rashid, 55, Mohammed Saleem, 47, Sucklane Shah, 47, Amjad Mahmood, 54, Iftaq Hussain, 46, and Arshad Mohammed, 56, deny all the charges they face The complainants are referred to as Girl A, Girl B and Girl C for legal reasons. Earlier in the trial, prosecutor Rossano Scamardella KC claimed that Mr Rashid began 'buying her presents and even gave her money’

title: Bolton council tried to hold a meeting about 'respect', it did not go well

evidence_packet.title: Bolton council tried to hold a meeting about 'respect', it did not go well
evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Bolton council tried to hold a meeting about 'respect', it did not go well 'The people of Bolton will be appalled' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 18:06, 03 Sep 2026 Updated 21:40, 03 Sep 2026 View 2 Images The meeting took pla There were heated scenes at
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Bolton council tried to hold a meeting about 'respect', it did not go well 'The people of Bolton will be appalled' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 18:06, 03 Sep 2026 Updated 21:40, 03 Sep 2026 View 2 Images The meeting took pla There were heated scenes at
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton council tried to hold a meeting about 'respect', it did not go well 'The people of Bolton will be appalled' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 18:06, 03 Sep 2026 Updated 21:40, 03 Sep 2026 View 2 Images The meeting took pla There were heated scenes at Bolton town hall as a debate about creating a more ‘respectful’ political atmosphere in the town descended into 'screaming in and playground behaviour' Following the unsavoury meeting, one councillor said ‘the people of Bolton watching this will be appalled’ as voices were raised and the mayor, Mohammed Iqbal, called for order several times Angry exchanges came during the debate about rising ‘hostility, abuse and intimidation towards elected members’, with a pledge made by all parties to support the Local Government Association’s ‘Debate Not Hate’ initiative Towards the end of the debate, as Jackie Schofield, a Labour councillor, was starting her speech, shouting could be heard between the Reform UK and Labour benches, prompted by an earlier reference to the Makerfield by-election Coun Schofield said: “I feel like I’m in a school playground, you really need to grow up. You really need to think about why you’re here and why you were elected to this role. The people of Bolton watching this will be appalled. That’s everybody, across every party.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bee Network Selfies and smiles as Andy Burnham hands President Macron special Manchester gift Exclusive images show how the pair smiled for a selfie after Macron received his gift View 5 Images "This is a very strong relationship" News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 17:57, 03 Sep 2026 Updated 22:19, 03 Sep 2026 Exclusive pictures show the moment Prime Minister Andy Burnham handed President Macron of France a very special Manchester-themed gift during a visit to Downing Street The former mayor of Greater Manchester often wears a similar Bee Network badge as a proud emblem of bus deregulation and transport improvements while he was in charge of the region. And this afternoon, PM Burnham wasted no time in handing out a similar decoration as he hosted his The badge features a worker bee which has long been an emblem of Manchester. And President Macron appeared to love it, as our exclusive pictures show He quickly took out his phone and took a selfie picture whilst wearing his new badge before giving it a resounding thumbs up, with a beaming Burnham just behind him. It was a light-hearted end to a serious day of talks in which the pair discussed the small boats crisis View 5 Images The former mayor of Greater Manchester often wears a similar Bee Network badge

About 800 barrels of the stout, estimated to be worth around £115,000, were taken from an industrial estate in Runcorn on Monday, Cheshire Constabulary has revealed. They were o The force said it was hoping for a 'full recovery of the stolen items' and has appealed for witnesses who may have seen a lorry entering the Aston Lane area at about 7.45pm The lorry is said to have connected to an HGV trailer containing the Guinness and left the site at about 7.55pm in the direction of the Mersey Gateway bridge A second lorry arrived at the same site at 9.12pm and connected to another trailer, which also contained barrels of Guinness, before leaving at 9.30pm in the direction of Rainhill and Watkinson Way, police said The stolen barrels, containing around 70,400 pints of the Irish tipple, had been intended to be delivered to pubs

The 55-year-old was sadly pronounced dead by emergency services at the scene, the British Transport P Police said previously that enquiries were underway to 'establish the full circumstances of what happened'. His family said he worked as a teacher for 25 years and 'went the extra mile again and again' during his career In full, the tribute said: "Simon was a devoted husband, a loving father of two, and a much-loved member of our family. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheshire Police Cheshire detective whose secret actions were 'beyond belief' is barred from policing forever The cop at Cheshire Police has been dismissed for gross misconduct Comments News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 06:03, 04 Sep 2026 View Image A detective who looked up information about a suspect being investigated by someone else and then trying to prevent criminal charges has been sacked for gross misconduct The detective inspector at Cheshire Police, whose name and gender have been kept secret, was sacked by the force's chief constable, Mark Roberts, following a misconduct hearing last month The unnamed officer involved themselves in an investigation which had nothing to do with them where they knew the family of the suspect and creating a 'conflict of interest', according to a published ruling The DI was said to have kept their relationship with the family secret from colleagues and then 'attempted to influence the investigation and outcome' in February 2026 The officer emailed the mother of the suspect and accessed police computer systems for information about the case 'without a legitimate policing purpose'

evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Bolton council tried to hold a meeting about 'respect', it did not go well 'The people of Bolton will be appalled' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 18:06, 03 Sep 2026 Updated 21:40, 03 Sep 2026 View 2 Images The meeting took pla There were heated scenes at
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Bolton council tried to hold a meeting about 'respect', it did not go well 'The people of Bolton will be appalled' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 18:06, 03 Sep 2026 Updated 21:40, 03 Sep 2026 View 2 Images The meeting took pla There were heated scenes at
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton council tried to hold a meeting about 'respect', it did not go well 'The people of Bolton will be appalled' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 18:06, 03 Sep 2026 Updated 21:40, 03 Sep 2026 View 2 Images The meeting took pla There were heated scenes at Bolton town hall as a debate about creating a more ‘respectful’ political atmosphere in the town descended into 'screaming in and playground behaviour' Following the unsavoury meeting, one councillor said ‘the people of Bolton watching this will be appalled’ as voices were raised and the mayor, Mohammed Iqbal, called for order several times Angry exchanges came during the debate about rising ‘hostility, abuse and intimidation towards elected members’, with a pledge made by all parties to support the Local Government Association’s ‘Debate Not Hate’ initiative Towards the end of the debate, as Jackie Schofield, a Labour councillor, was starting her speech, shouting could be heard between the Reform UK and Labour benches, prompted by an earlier reference to the Makerfield by-election Coun Schofield said: “I feel like I’m in a school playground, you really need to grow up. You really need to think about why you’re here and why you were elected to this role. The people of Bolton watching this will be appalled. That’s everybody, across every party.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics Angela Rayner to set up antisemitism committee amid spate of hate crimes against Jewish community "Right now, the levels of anxiety are really quite high and probably never higher in terms of a sense of people’s personal safety" News Sophie W A Cabinet committee on antisemitism will be set up to address concerns over a spate of hate crimes against the Jewish community, Angela Rayner has announced The plan was unveiled by the Housing, Communities and Local Government Secretary today (September 3) during a roundtable in Downing Street with leaders from the community. The Prime Minister, Andy Burnham acknowledged “how much the community is struggling” He told the gathering: “Right now, the levels of anxiety are really quite high and probably never higher in terms of a sense of people’s personal safety.” Leaders of Jewish organisations told the Prime Minister and Ms Rayner that measures were needed to address the community’s heightened fears heading into the Jewish holiday season, a year on from the Manchester synagogue terror attack Melvin Cravitz, 66, and Adrian Daulby, 53, were killed when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, drove into the gates of the synagogue on October 2 2025 and began attacking with a knife while wearing a fake suicide belt

evidence_packet.summary: Manchester synagogue attack Bid to block 'MI5 material' on Manchester synagogue terror attack as new details emerge A public inquiry into the tragedy could now be established over 'sensitive' MI5 evidence News Paul Britton Reporter 16:23, 03 Sep 2026 The Home Secretary wants to b
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester synagogue attack Bid to block 'MI5 material' on Manchester synagogue terror attack as new details emerge A public inquiry into the tragedy could now be established over 'sensitive' MI5 evidence News Paul Britton Reporter 16:23, 03 Sep 2026 The Home Secretary wants to block a 'discreet body of MI5 material' from being publicly disclosed at an inquest into the deaths of two men killed when terrorist Jihad Al-Shamie attacked a Manchester synagogue last year If Chief Coroner, Judge Alexia Durran, upholds the application by Shabana Mahmood, a public inquiry into the attack in Crumpsall on Yom Kippur could ultimately be established. A 'closed session' of a pre-inquest review to assess further details will be held at a later date, with Questions over whether or not Al-Shamie was known to the security services before the attack on October 2 last year also emerged during a pre-inquest review hearing held on Thursday Security guard Melvin Cravitz, 66, and Adrian Daulby, 53, were killed at the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation synagogue View 6 Images The synagogue in Crumpsall (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Metropolitan University Manchester Metropolitan University accused of 'pure hypocrisy' over land row The university has come under fire from a councillor about its plans for Ryebank Fields Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter Manchester Metropolitan University (MMU) has been accused of ‘pure hypocrisy’ in a row over its plans to flog Ryebank Fields in Chorlton for developers to build new homes Chantal Kerr-Sheppard, a Green Party councillor in Chorlton, said MMU promoted a ‘biodiversity’ campaign in May called Make a Metre Matter, which encouraged people to ‘plant and [make] green spaces’, while at the same time pressing ahead with its own plans to sell off a large pat A planning application led by MMU along with Step Places and Southway Housing Trust is aiming to build 120 homes on Ryebank Fields. If approved, the job would involve work to fix the land’s ‘contamination with asbestos, heavy metals and hazardous hydrocarbons’, MMU said Councillor Kerr-Sheppard said the planning reports to build homes on Ryebank Fields, which are published online and have been seen by the Local Democracy Reporting Service, showed it would mean a ‘40 per cent net loss in biodiversity’ for animal habitats in the area The planning reports also showed the application to build on the land would need ‘offsite mitigation’ to make up for the changes

Tahir Rashid, 55, Mohammed Saleem, 47, Sucklane Shah, 47, Amjad Mahmood, 54, Iftaq Hussain, 46, and Arshad Mohammed, 56, deny all the charges they face The complainants are referred to as Girl A, Girl B and Girl C for legal reasons. The alleged abuse of Girl C is claimed to have taken place in the late 1980s, with the alleged ‘exploitation’ of Girl A and B said to have occurred in the mid-2000s Girl C was allegedly abused by Mr Rashid, described by prosecutors as the ‘undoubted ringleader in this group’, who also allegedly abused Girl A and B, after Girl C moved to Rochdale in the late 1980s Mr Rashid, also known as 'Taz,' was 19 years old at the time and 'very well built,' Minshull Street Crown Court has heard. Earlier in the trial, prosecutor Rossano Scamardella KC claimed that Mr Rashid began 'buying her presents and even gave her money’

evidence_packet.title: The Mancunian Way: Worst road in Manchester?
evidence_packet.lead: “A lot of cars park on single yellow or double yellow, and people don’t understand why they’re getting a ticket, they’ll plead with you just to give them one more minute.
evidence_packet.summary: “A lot of cars park on single yellow or double yellow, and people don’t understand why they’re getting a ticket, they’ll plead with you just to give them one more minute. It can be very difficult,” he told my colleague Declan Carey, who visited the stretch this week While there D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: “A lot of cars park on single yellow or double yellow, and people don’t understand why they’re getting a ticket, they’ll plead with you just to give them one more minute. It can be very difficult,” he told my colleague Declan Carey, who visited the stretch this week While there Declan heard car horns blaring, pedestrians veering wildly into the road and plenty of road rage. Dubbed Manchester’s ‘worst’ road, many shopkeepers told Declan they’ve seen accidents and deaths on the ‘horrendous’ road since the 1990s “It’s one of the worst roads in Manchester, it’s total chaos in the evenings,” the traffic warden adds View 6 Images Traffic chaos Stockport Road in Longsight. Picture Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News (Image: Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News) Data kept by Transport for Greater Manchester points to a major safety problem on Stockport Road. A fatality happened in 2025 at the ever-busy junction with Slade Lane Further up by Stanley Road and Dickenson Road, the area is littered with accident reports, with multiple minor and serious collisions logged since 2024. But can anything really be done to improve things?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tameside 'Enough is enough': Children sent home from Tameside school 'for second day' in bitter uniform row 'It's ridiculous. It's absolutely ridiculous. They’re treating the kids like prisoners, it’s an absolute joke' News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 1 The parent of a pupil at a Tameside school at the centre of a uniform row says his daughter was sent home for a second day in a row today (September 3) A dad-of-one, he slammed Denton Community Academy over its 'absolutely ridiculous' uniform policy, which saw him shell out a 'fortune' on a new, longer skirt last night. But he says she was still turned away for a second day The school first came under fire from another parent yesterday (September 2) after pupils were turned away on the first day back after summer for having skirts 'a couple of inches' above the knee . The 51-year-old dad, speaking to the Manchester Evening News today, said he bought View 4 Images A screenshot from the school's uniform book (Image: Denton Community Academy/Northern Education Trust ) However, after his daughter has missed another day of school, he said he has 'had enough' and the school are treating the pupils 'like prisoners'. He said: "I’ve just had enough today. My daughter’s been turned away again for the same reason

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The family are Altrincham FC season ticket holders Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Lois (second right) with husband Ollie and kids Imogen and Jacob A local mum of two is fighting for her life in hospital after a liver transplant that almost killed her Lois Kinder, 44, was rushed to hospital in mid-July after becoming critically ill with acute liver failure. Within days she was placed in an induced coma and transferred to the specialist liver intensive care unit at Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, one of only a handful of c On 22 July a donor liver became available, but during the operation she suffered three cardiac arrests after a blood clot blocked the main artery to her lungs, leaving her starved of oxygen for a prolonged period. Surgeons told her husband Ollie more than once that she was unlike Against the odds she pulled through. Six weeks on she is conscious and recognises her family, but the lack of oxygen caused significant brain damage to both sides of her brain. She cannot move, remains on a ventilator and dialysis, and is still in critical care “She’s conscious. She is recognising who we are,” Ollie said. “She’s saying the odd word, albeit very, very weak. She can’t move or anything like that at the moment. They’re hopeful of a form of recovery, but whether she will walk again remains unknown.”

A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Quays is Greater Manchester's unique waterfront destination, situated just 15 minutes by tram from Manchester city centre. It is Britain's hottest short-break destination and packs everything you can do in a big city into one spectacular square mile. Shopping, sport, art, dra Live theatre, the best of cinema and one of the country's finest museums: The Quays offers a fantastic choice of things to do and see. Imperial War Museum North and The Lowry are vibrant and exciting examples of contemporary architecture, the contents as stunning as the setting a Whether you're a shopaholic or just someone who likes a bargain, the opening of the Quayside MediaCityUK has made The Quays a mecca for the discerning shopper with big-name brand shops and stores offering discount prices - up to 70 per cent lower than the high street - all year r There's no better place to find top sport action than The Quays. Home to two of the most renowned clubs in British sport - Manchester United and Lancashire County Cricket Club , The Quays is the area to head for when wanting the best in football and cricket. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Our Mayor is now our Prime Minister, and the skills agenda he's brought to Downing Street is one we've lived and breathed for over a decade Andy Burnham has spent some of his first fortnight in office setting out plans to reshape technical education and get more young people into work, built on the MBacc model developed here in Greater Manchester. This is familiar ground for us. For over ten years Manchester Digital That gap has become harder to bridge, economic uncertainty, higher costs and cautious hiring are playing their part as is AI, which is starting to strip out the routine tasks junior roles were built on. evidence_packet.summary: The football schedules may be playing a bigger part than Oasis fans realise, as Noel Gallagher confirms that the band are set to fill the void in summer 2027
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Music & Nightlife Noel Gallagher confirms summer 2027 for Oasis tour return - as football schedules align The football schedules may be playing a bigger part than Oasis fans realise, as Noel Gallagher confirms that the band are set to fill the void in summer 2027 Commen Noel Gallagher has given the strongest confirmation yet that Oasis are to make a big summer 2027 return to the live music arena. Noel had remained tight-lipped about the new tour rumours in recent months, while brother Liam Gallagher has been teasing fans with lots of hints and c However now, in his own words, Noel has confirmed there's "something happening" in summer 2027. Speaking to TalkSport presenter Andy Goldstein on Wednesday night, there was plenty of banter about brother Liam's recent departure from social media site X Liam had urged Noel on X to announce a new tour, saying: "Ffs RKID announce the tour we’re all losing our minds." He then went on to say he was quitting social media amid apparent frustrations about the "goose chases" around the new tour rumours As the MEN revealed earlier this summer , the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, home to the Gallaghers' beloved Manchester City, is set to host up to 12 gigs from Oasis across June 2027. Man City's games conclude at the end of May, giving Oasis free reign to take over the ground for The MEN understands from music industry sources that the gig schedule will see three gigs a week, including weekends, at the Etihad Stadium across June, while plans are also afoot to stage a huge return to Knebworth from the band later in the summer

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
